speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I understand your 8-month-old son is experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. Can you describe his bowel movements, specifically if they are frequent, watery, or contain mucus or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the baby pass gas or stool after crying, and does he seem to pull his legs up toward his abdomen? I also need to know if there has been any vomiting, particularly if it is green or yellow in color.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Has he passed any stool recently, and if so, what was the consistency and color? I also need to know if his abdomen feels firm or hard to the touch when you gently press on it.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to check for signs of obstruction. Has he passed any meconium in the first 48 hours of life, and does he pass thin, ribbon-like stools now? I will also request an abdominal X-ray to look for dilated bowel loops. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of dilated bowel segments with an air-fluid level and absence of rectal gas strongly suggest a distal obstruction. I need to perform a rectal exam to check for a "blast" of stool or a tight sphincter, which would be diagnostic for Hirschsprung disease. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of failure to thrive, abdominal distension, and delayed stool passage, combined with X-ray evidence of a distal obstruction, is highly suggestive of Hirschsprung disease. I will now perform a rectal exam to assess for a tight anal sphincter and the characteristic "explosive" stool release upon withdrawal.

speaker: Doctor
